title: Jack Lane sidemen, Eddie Falk and the American Brass Band drummers
summary: He remembers Bach Kay as no crackerjack and calls Falk the best clarinetist; his brother played bass drum and the professor cared most about tuba and bass drum time.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I was going to ask about a couple of fellas that played with Jack Lane. Do you remember Dave Perkins?
Or a shield Bach Kay. A clarinet player. With the name of Bach Kay. Do you remember? Played with Jack Lane a long time.
Bach Kay. I used to remember him. Yeah. But he wasn't no crackerjack. But the best clarinet player that ever I played with was a boy by the name of Eddie Falk.
He came up in that American Brass Band.
Yeah. Is that right? That's a fact. That's a lot.
Oh do you remember some more members of that band? Who were the drummers? Did they use the bass and snare drum? How many drummers would they use?
My oldest brother used to play bass drum. Oh he did? Yeah.
They had another snare drummer too?

Yeah we had a snare drummer but he didn't stick at it very long. And then we got another fella. But they didn't, the professor wasn't much worried about no drummer. He was more worried about the blowing instruments you see. The tuba player and the bass drum player because they're the ones that's got to be correct with that time beat you see. To keep a band from running away or going above the time that the piece is played in. And that's what lots of bands do. And dances especially.
